formulations.label: Vaginal tablet
formulations.strengths: Clinic product: 1000 mg. UK product found: 600 mg vaginal capsule (also 200 mg capsules and 2% vaginal cream).
formulations.note: No UK 1000 mg fenticonazole vaginal tablet was found (emc and MHRA Products searched). Content here comes from the UK SPC for fenticonazole 600 mg vaginal capsules; its dose (one 600 mg capsule once) does not apply to the 1000 mg tablet. Systemic absorption after vaginal use is minimal.

src.q: Each vaginal capsule contains 600 mg of the active ingredient fenticonazole nitrate.
systemic absorption of fenticonazole nitrate after vaginal administration is minimal.

bnf.note: BNF/BNFC is only available in the UK; not accessed.

src.q: Treatment of vulvovaginal candidiasis.

restrictions.note: No prescribing restriction in the UK fenticonazole 600 mg vaginal capsule SPC. No emc entry, BUMPS leaflet or SPS page found for fenticonazole.

items.t: UK 600 mg vaginal capsule, adults: one capsule once only, at bedtime, inserted deep into the vagina. No UK dosing found for the 1000 mg vaginal tablet.

src.q: Adults: One 600 mg vaginal capsule once only, at bedtime. The capsule must be introduced deeply into the vagina.

items.t: Not established under 16 years (no data). From 16 years: adult dose.

src.q: The safety and efficacy of Gynoxin children under 16 years have not been established.
The dose recommendation for children aged 16 years or above is the same as for adults.

items.t: Hypersensitivity to fenticonazole or any excipient. Peanut or soya allergy (the UK 600 mg capsule contains soya lecithin; check the excipients of the product supplied).

src.q: Hypersensitivity to the active substance or to any of the excipients listed in section 6.1.
This medicinal product should not be used in patients allergic to peanut or soya.

items.t: Advise the patient to see a doctor if: no relief within a week; more than 2 infections in 6 months; STI history or exposure; age over 60; known allergy to imidazoles or other vaginal antifungals; abnormal vaginal bleeding or blood-stained discharge; vulval/vaginal sores, ulcers or blisters; lower abdominal pain or dysuria; rash or itching after use.

src.q: the symptoms have not been relieved within one week
known hypersensitivity to imidazoles or other vaginal antifungal products

items.t: Do not use with barrier contraceptives, spermicides, douches or other vaginal products. Parabens may cause (delayed) allergic reactions; stop if sensitisation occurs.

src.q: The vaginal capsules should not be used in conjunction with barrier contraceptives, spermicides, intravaginal douches or other vaginal products
Should local sensitisation or an allergic reaction occur, the treatment should be discontinued.

items.t: Treat the partner if also infected.

src.q: Appropriate therapy is indicated when the partner is also infected.

items.t: No interaction studies. Oils in the capsule can damage latex contraceptives; local vaginal treatment may inactivate spermicides (not recommended together). No systemic interactions with master-list medicines are stated.

src.q: Fat excipients and oils contained in the vaginal capsules could damage contraceptives made of latex.
any local vaginal treatment is likely to inactivate a local contraceptive spermicide.

renal.note: No renal statement in the UK fenticonazole 600 mg vaginal capsule SPC; systemic absorption is minimal.

hepatic.note: No hepatic statement in the UK fenticonazole 600 mg vaginal capsule SPC.

items.t: Limited human data; low systemic exposure expected. Use in pregnancy only under a doctor's supervision.

src.q: There are a limited amount of data from the use of fenticonazole in pregnant women.
Fenticonazole should be used in pregnancy under the supervision of a physician.

items.t: Significant transfer to milk not expected, but no human data; use during breastfeeding only under a doctor's supervision.

src.q: any significant transfer into breast milk is not expected.
Fenticonazole should be used during the lactation under the supervision of a physician.

items.t: May damage latex condoms/diaphragms: use other contraceptive methods during treatment. No effect on fertility in animal studies.

src.q: Patients should be advised to use alternative contraceptive methods/precautions while using this product.
animal studies have not demonstrated any effects of the drug on fertility.

items.t: A mild, transient burning sensation may occur after application; systemic effects are not expected.

src.q: A mild, transient burning sensation may occur after application.
systemic undesirable reactions are not expected.

items.t: Allergic reaction or local sensitisation (rash, itching, erythema): stop treatment.

src.q: Should local sensitisation or an allergic reaction occur, the treatment should be discontinued.

items.t: Review if symptoms are not relieved within one week.

src.q: the symptoms have not been relieved within one week

items.t: Insert deep into the vagina at bedtime; it washes off with water.

src.q: The capsule must be introduced deeply into the vagina.

items.t: Do not use condoms, diaphragms, spermicides or douches during treatment; see a doctor if not better within a week.
